In [[statistics]], a '''record value''' or '''record statistic''' is the largest or smallest value obtained from a sequence of random variables. The theory is closely related to that used in [[order statistics]].<ref>{{Cite book | first1 = Mohammad | last1 = Ahsanullah| first2 = Valery B. | last2 = Nevzorov| doi = 10.1007/978-3-642-04898-2_482 | chapter = Record Statistics | title = International Encyclopedia of Statistical Science | pages = 1195 | year = 2011 | isbn = 978-3-642-04897-5 
}}</ref>

The term was first introduced by K. N. Chandler in 1952.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Chandler | first1 = K. N. | year = 1952 | title = The Distribution and Frequency of Record Values | journal = [[Journal of the Royal Statistical Society. Series B (Methodological)]] | volume = 14 | issue = 2 | pages = 220–228  | publisher = [[Royal Statistical Society]] | jstor = 2983870}}</ref>
